 Oral Judgment

Heard Sri.Lokesh Malavalli, learned counsel for the appellants, Sri.N.R.Jagadeeswara, learned counsel for respondent No.2 and Sri.T.P.Malipatil, learned Additional Government Advocate for respondent No.1.
2.
Though the matter is listed for admission, with the consent of parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. Appellant's land in Sy.No.66 has been acquired for the construction of Aluru tank.
13 acres of the land has been lost for the said project.
Acquisition and determination of the compensation at the rate of NC: 2024:KHC:32989 Rs.16,000/- by the Land Acquisition Officer is not in dispute.
4. Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation, appellants herein filed an application under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act.

5. Learned Judge in the reference Court considered the oral and documentary evidence placed on record including the records of rights extracts, the other material documents namely existence of borewell, the electricity consumption charges and estimate given by the APMC, Davangere for the relevant period of time and enhanced compensation from Rs.16,000/- to Rs.80,000/- per acre.

sentences.text: 6. Being not satisfied by the determination of the compensation, appellants herein filed an appeal before the First Appellate Court in MA No.224/2011.

7. Learned Judge in the First Appellate Court after reappreciation of the material evidence placed on record, NC: 2024:KHC:32989 redetermined the compensation in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- as against sum of Rs.80,000/- awarded by the reference Court.
8. Being not satisfied with the said enhancement, appellants are before this Court, in this appeal.

9. Sri.Lokesh Malavalli, learned counsel for the appellants reiterating the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum, vehemently contended that the land in question was admittedly a fertile and irrigated land and appellants herein were growing DCH cotton as the main crop, apart from growing ragi, maize, vegetables and sunflower.
Therefore, determination of the compensation in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- awarded by the First Appellate Court is on the lower side and sought for reasonable enhancement.

10. He also pointed out that according to the relevant market value in and round the vicinity and also the profit that the appellants were deriving from the lands, atleast sum of Rs.2,45,000/- is to be determined as the NC: 2024:KHC:32989 compensation to the acquired land and sought for allowing the appeal.
11. Sri

.T.P.Maliptail, learned Additional Government Advocate and Sri.N.R.Jagadeeswara, learned counsel supports the order passed by the First Appellate Court by contending that material evidence placed on record has been properly appreciated by both the Courts and sought for dismissal of the appeal.
12.
Having heard the parties in detail, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.

13. On such perusal of the material on record, it is crystal clear that at an undisputed point of time,
original land owners namely Rudrappa and Lingaraju issued a letter to the Land Acquisition Officer vide Ex.P.17.
14.
In Ex.P.17, there is no mention of growing cotton, ragi, sunflower, vegetables and other crops.
Ex .P.17 contains only existence of coconut, mango trees and areca nut trees in the land.
Ex.P.17 also mentions about the growing of mulberry for the purpose of sericulture.

16. However, while adducing the evidence before the reference Court, all together a different stand has been taken by the appellants herein to the effect that in the acquired land, crops like DCH cotton, ragi, maize, vegetables and sunflower were raised.
The acquired land had the facility of the water source by way of a tube well and the electricity connection to the said tube well was obtained and necessary documents were placed on record.

sentences.text:
Based on the oral and documentary evidence placed on record, learned Judge in the reference Court enhanced the compensation insofar as land value is concerned by adopting the capitalization method from Rs.16,000/- to Rs.80,000/-.
18.

There is a detailed discussion in the order passed by the learned Judge in the reference Court to the effect that the oral testimony of P.W.1 to 3 would only go to show that they could raise only one crop in a year NC: 2024:KHC:32989 though they deposed before the Court that they were growing two crops in a year.
19. Apart from the RTC extract, no other documents were placed on record for having sold the raised crops in the APMC.
20. However, learned Judge in the First Appellate Court reappreciated the material evidence on record and enhanced the compensation in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- as against sum of Rs.80,000/-.
21. Sri

.Lokesh Malavalli, learned counsel contended that in the absence of proper proof being placed on record with regard to the second crop being grown, taking note of the fact that second crop could only be grown in summer, at least 50% of the value of the first crop to be adjudged here and same be taken note of and sought for enhancement in a sum of Rs.40,000/- over and above sum of Rs.1,00,000/- awarded by the First Appellate Court.
Learned counsel for the respondents opposed for the same.

23. Taking note of the rival contentions of the parties and reappreciation of the material on record, if not to the entire extent, having regard to the fact that the land had the irrigation facility, some crops or vegetables would have been grown in the summer as well, it would be just and proper to enhance the compensation in a sum of Rs.1,25,000/- per acre as against sum of Rs.16,000/- awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer, enhanced to Rs.80,000/- by the reference Court and further enhanced to sum of Rs.1,00,000/- by the First Appellate Court.

24. Further, since it is an isolated acquisition, for the purpose of construction of the tank,
respondents would not also be affected by suitably enhancing the compensation in the case of the appellants.

25. Accordingly, the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:32989 ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
ii. Claimants are entitled to sum of Rs.1,25,000/- as compensation with all consequential benefits and costs.
